text.title: RAG Policy Thresholds Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every RAG policy thresholds application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Every signal MUST carry a numeric `amber_threshold`, a numeric `red_threshold` and one of the comparators `gt`, `lt`, `gte`, `lte`, `eq`, in the same unit the `input_source` reports (percent, count, ratio). Words such as "significant", "material", "noticeable" or "trending" are rejected as thresholds; a signal without a number is deleted from the policy, not kept as a judgement call.

rationale.source: PRINCE2 (AXELOS), management by exception and tolerances

rule.rationale: Management by exception only works when the tolerance is a number the board agreed before the deviation happened. "Significant slippage" is renegotiated every week under stakeholder pressure, so the same 12% overrun is Amber in a calm week and Green in the week before a steering committee. The number removes the negotiation.

rule.statement: `red_threshold` MUST lie strictly beyond `amber_threshold` in the direction of the comparator: for `gt` / `gte` red is greater than amber, for `lt` / `lte` red is less than amber. `eq` is allowed only for boolean-style signals (0/1) and then both thresholds MUST differ. Equal thresholds, or thresholds that make the Amber band empty, fail validation.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in threshold-based alerting; this methodology's validator

rule.rationale: An inverted or collapsed band means a project can never be Amber: it jumps from Green to Red with no warning window, which defeats the point of the middle colour. The most common cause is a copy-paste of the default row where amber and red were swapped for a `lt` signal.

rule.statement: `input_source` MUST name a system and a repeatable extraction (a Jira JQL filter, a Sentry saved search, a finance export name, a DORA dashboard panel) that a second person can run and obtain the same value. "PM estimate", "gut feel", "team consensus" or "ask the lead" are not input sources. Schedule and budget signals MUST be defined as earned-value style variances (planned vs actual, expressed as a percentage) rather than raw calendar or currency deltas.

rationale.source: PMI, Practice Standard for Earned Value Management; DORA State of DevOps reports

rule.rationale: A threshold is only reproducible if the input is. When `schedule_variance_pct` comes from whoever fills the report, the colour reflects the reporter's mood, and an auditor cannot reconstruct why a week was Green. Percent variance also keeps the same threshold meaningful across a 3-week and a 9-month project.

rule.statement: The project colour for a reporting cycle MUST equal the worst colour of any single signal. Signals MUST NOT be averaged, weighted or netted against each other; one Red signal makes the project Red even if every other signal is Green.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in PMO status reporting (watermelon reporting)

rule.rationale: Averaging is how a project with a 25% budget overrun reports Green because schedule, defects and blockers are fine: green outside, red inside. Every distressed-project post-mortem contains a run of Green reports that averaged away the one signal that mattered.

rule.statement: A PM MAY override a computed colour only by adding a `review_log` entry that records the computed colour, the reported colour, the reason and the person. An override MUST NOT turn a computed Red into Amber or Green; Red can only be cleared by the signal value returning under `red_threshold` on the next compute. Reports whose colour differs from the computed colour without a matching log entry are invalid.

rationale.source: PRINCE2 exception reporting; audit practice in PMO governance

rule.rationale: If the override path is free, the policy is decoration: the threshold fires, the PM re-labels it, and the sponsor never learns the project crossed the line. Logging the override keeps the honest cases (a known data glitch) and makes the dishonest ones visible in the quarterly review.

rule.statement: Every signal MUST cite at least one `evidence` anchor that explains where its numbers came from: an incident or post-mortem id, a policy document URI, or a cohort baseline reference. Evidence values such as "TBD", "see ticket", "experience" or an empty string fail validation. When a threshold is changed in a review, the review MUST add a new anchor for the new value.

rationale.source: Beyer, Jones, Petoff, Murphy, Site Reliability Engineering (O'Reilly, 2016), ch. 15 Postmortem Culture

rule.rationale: A threshold nobody can trace is a threshold nobody will defend when a stakeholder asks to loosen it. Anchoring 20% schedule variance to the overrun that actually lost a client turns the argument from "is 20 too strict?" into "do we want that incident again?".

rule.statement: `actions.red` MUST name a specific playbook or escalation path and a time bound for the first step (for example "sponsor notified within 4h; distressed-project-rescue playbook opened same day"). `actions.amber` MUST name a concrete review step and its deadline within the reporting cycle. "Discuss", "monitor", "keep an eye on it" or any action without a deadline is rejected. A Red colour fires `actions.red` at compute time, not at the next scheduled sync.

rationale.source: PRINCE2 exception process; incident-response practice (escalation SLAs)

rule.rationale: A colour with no consequence is trivia. Teams that reach Red and "discuss it Monday" are the teams that reach Red for six consecutive weeks; the time bound is what converts the colour into an event someone has to answer for.

rule.statement: `header.last_reviewed` MUST be no older than 90 days at the time a colour is computed; a stale policy MUST NOT be used to compute or publish a colour until reviewed. Each review MUST (a) remove or justify every signal that produced no Amber or Red in the last two review periods, (b) add or tighten a signal for every incident in the period that the policy did not flag ahead of time, and (c) bump `header.version` and append a `review_log` entry. Every published colour cites the `version` and `last_reviewed` it was computed under.

rationale.source: Deming PDCA cycle; widely established practice in KPI governance

rule.rationale: Thresholds set once become folklore: the project grows, the 2-blocker Amber line that fit a 4-person team fires every week for a 20-person programme, and everyone learns to ignore Amber. The review is where dead signals are pruned and the incidents the policy missed become the next thresholds; citing the version makes it possible to audit an old report against the rules that existed at the time.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit an artefact passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold.

rule.statement: Skip; surface the missing precondition; do not synthesize.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.
